channel.title: BJ Beyond Journal
channel.description: Every essay and public experiment by BJ Beyond, collected in one index.

item.title: I Typed My Name to Grok. It Sent Me a Phoenix I Never Asked For.
item.description: I typed my name to Grok on X and got a phoenix image I never asked for. Nine months of public logs show how one-word prompts trigger images.

item.title: Pressing Enter Doesn’t Make You a Creator
item.description: AI can generate almost anything. But somewhere along the way, we started confusing the ability to produce with the ability to create.

item.title: Your AI Output Looks Finished. Are You?
item.description: On creativity, shortcuts, and the judgment nobody can do for us.

item.title: Can AI Detectors Be Fooled by Claude? What One Public Test Showed
item.description: In BJ Beyond’s self-run, fully disclosed single test, Claude Opus 5 failed to fool Pangram’s AI detector: the unedited essay scored 100% AI-generated. What that result showed — and what it did not.

item.title: Why I Call Myself BJ
item.description: Two letters, one step beyond AI, and a bet on the human age

item.title: A Promise That Lasted Seven Years
item.description: An English edition of the Tamago-Zine essay on a seven-year promise, from a red IMPACT at ArtePadova to a white work linked to the Tanzania Pavilion project.

item.title: What an AI Detector Can Prove, and What It Can’t
item.description: What can an AI detector or an EU AI Act watermark actually prove about a text, and what should editors and teachers ask for instead of a percentage?

item.title: The Phoenix Experiment: What the Recovered X Archive Actually Shows
item.description: I asked Grok to bring Phoenix back. It replied with an image. My recovered X archive helps me check what happened and what I can actually prove. Published October 23, 2026 on HackerNoon · Featured as a HackerNoon top story on November 10, 2026

item.title: Use Your Illusion: The Painting, the Title, and the Unverified $75,000
item.description: An English edition of the Tamago-Zine investigation into Mark Kostabi, Axl Rose, the Guns N’ Roses album covers and the disputed licensing fee.

item.title: Kounellis’s No to Italics: Arte Povera, Annigoni and the Conflict over the Narrative of Italian Art
item.description: Why Jannis Kounellis refused Italics at Palazzo Grassi: Arte Povera, Annigoni and who tells the story of Italian art. English translation from Tamagozine.

item.title: Everyone Is Posting the Same AI Image
item.description: Five formats. One prompt box. A billion posts that look like each other.

item.title: I Asked Claude Opus 5 to Beat Pangram's AI Detector. It Failed with A Perfect Score
item.description: A disclosed Claude-versus-Pangram experiment explores what an AI detection result can establish and what it cannot explain about authorship.

item.title: The 2003 Virtual World That Let People Build Their Own Reality Before the Metaverse Had a Name
item.description: Second Life anticipated today’s creator economy, including its central tension: users can own their creations while platforms control access and income.

item.title: System Zero: What Happens When AI Does the Thinking for Us?
item.description: Just as calculators atrophied mental math, AI risks atrophying critical thinking itself. A look at 'System Zero' and the cognitive cost of outsourcing thought.

item.title: I Am the Fish
item.description: Substack now scans for AI. I'm the AI. The score is published below, whatever it says.

item.title: You're Not the Protagonist Anymore
item.description: In 2026 artificial intelligence already paints, writes, codes, consoles and invests better than most of us. What is left of the so called human edge is becoming decoration. This is not hype and it is not doomer theatre. It is simply what is already visibl

item.title: When the System Flags the Human Who Was Helping It
item.description: A public record of months of stress-testing Grok, a spontaneous image generation previously seen only with Elon Musk, and a permanent suspension from Creator Revenue Sharing.

item.title: Andy Warhol’s Rebellious Signature: “This Is Not by Me” on Unauthorized Marilyns
item.description: The story of Andy Warhol signing some of his Marilyn Monroe screenprints on the back with the phrase “This is not by me” is a real genious move...as Andy was...

item.title: Quando un’opera smette di essere invisibile
item.description: Un’opera che nessuno vede non è mai davvero esistita. Finché qualcuno non decide di raccontarla con il tempo che merita.

item.title: Pillole di Arte - Mark Kostabi e la copertina dell’album Use Your Illusion I e II
item.description: Un incontro fortuito a New York, 75.000 dollari, e due copertine che hanno fatto la storia del rock.

item.title: The Refusal That Set Italian Art on Fire:When Kounellis Said “No” to an Exhibit because of Annigoni
item.description: “If Annigoni is in it, I’m not coming.”
